## Details

<a id="ia.webmcp-declarative"></a>

### 4.1 WebMCP declarative API

- Stable ID: `ia.webmcp-declarative`
- Stage: Act
- Strength: SHOULD
- AR practices: AR-ACT-07 (mapping: full)
- Evidence type: `recommendation`
- Fix: Annotate your main forms with WebMCP toolname and tooldescription attributes.
- Fix workflow: [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md#ia.webmcp-declarative)
- Evidence source: [agentready.org AR-ACT-07](https://www.agentready.org/#act)
- Applicability: detected_surface (mcp)
- Expected result: The HTML contains a form with toolname and tooldescription attributes
- Rescan: `isagentready results {domain} --checkpoint ia.webmcp-declarative`
- Details: https://isagentready.com/en/methodology/checkpoints/ia.webmcp-declarative

Why: WebMCP is the W3C proposal for exposing website functionality directly to AI agents. Declarative tool annotations on forms let agents perform actions (search, purchase, book) without screen scraping.

References:

- [WebMCP specification](https://webmachinelearning.github.io/webmcp/) (guide)
- [WebMCP Chrome Early Preview](https://developer.chrome.com/blog/webmcp-epp) (guide)

Steps:

1. Add toolname and tooldescription to each form that agents may use.

   ```html
   <form toolname="search" tooldescription="Search products by keyword">
     <input name="q" toolparamdescription="Search keywords">
   </form>
   ```
2. Or register tools in JavaScript with document.modelContext.registerTool().

   ```javascript
   document.modelContext.registerTool({
     name: "search",
     description: "Search products",
     inputSchema: {type: "object", properties: {q: {type: "string"}}},
     execute: async ({q}) => ({content: []})
   });
   ```

Verify:

```bash
curl -sf https://{domain}/
```

<a id="ia.a2a-agent-card"></a>

### 4.3 A2A Agent Card

- Stable ID: `ia.a2a-agent-card`
- Stage: Act
- Strength: MAY
- AR practices: AR-READ-06 (mapping: partial)
- Evidence type: `recommendation`
- Fix: Serve an A2A Agent Card with name, description, url, capabilities and supportedInterfaces.
- Fix workflow: [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md#ia.a2a-agent-card)
- Evidence source: [agentready.org AR-READ-06](https://www.agentready.org/#read)
- Applicability: detected_surface (api)
- Pass condition: JSON document with name, description, url, capabilities
- Expected result: exit code 0
- Rescan: `isagentready results {domain} --checkpoint ia.a2a-agent-card`
- Details: https://isagentready.com/en/methodology/checkpoints/ia.a2a-agent-card

Why: The Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol enables autonomous agent-to-agent communication. An Agent Card at /.well-known/agent-card.json advertises the agent's capabilities and supported A2A interfaces.

References:

- [A2A 1.0 specification](https://a2a-protocol.org/latest/specification/) (spec)

Steps:

1. Create /.well-known/agent-card.json with the required A2A 1.0 fields.

   ```json
   {
     "name": "Example agent",
     "description": "Answers questions about Example products",
     "url": "https://example.com/a2a",
     "version": "1.0.0",
     "capabilities": {"streaming": false},
     "supportedInterfaces": [{"url": "https://example.com/a2a", "protocolBinding": "JSONRPC"}],
     "skills": [{"id": "search", "name": "Search", "description": "Search the catalog"}]
   }
   ```
2. Serve the file as application/json with HTTP 200.

Verify:

```bash
curl -sf https://{domain}/.well-known/agent-card.json | jq -e '.name and .url'
```

<a id="ia.mcp-discovery"></a>

### 4.4 MCP discovery

- Stable ID: `ia.mcp-discovery`
- Stage: Act
- Strength: MAY
- AR practices: AR-ACT-03, AR-ACT-10 (mapping: partial)
- Evidence type: `scanner_data`
- Fix: Publish an MCP server card with serverInfo and a transport object.
- Fix workflow: [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md#ia.mcp-discovery)
- Evidence source: [agentready.org AR-ACT-03](https://www.agentready.org/#act)
- Applicability: detected_surface (api)
- Expected result: exit code 0
- Rescan: `isagentready results {domain} --checkpoint ia.mcp-discovery`
- Details: https://isagentready.com/en/methodology/checkpoints/ia.mcp-discovery

Why: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) by Anthropic is the standard for connecting AI assistants to external tools and data. A discovery document lets AI systems find and connect to your MCP server. SEP-1649 (modelcontextprotocol PR 2127) defines the new server-card.json schema with serverInfo, transport, and capabilities fields.

References:

- [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) (guide)
- [MCP specification](https://spec.modelcontextprotocol.io) (spec)
- [SEP-1649 server card](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/pull/2127) (guide)

Steps:

1. Create /.well-known/mcp/server-card.json with serverInfo.name and a transport.

   ```json
   {
     "serverInfo": {"name": "Example MCP", "version": "1.0.0"},
     "transport": {"type": "streamable-http", "endpoint": "https://example.com/mcp"}
   }
   ```
2. Link the MCP endpoint from llms.txt and the AI Catalog.

Verify:

```bash
curl -sf https://{domain}/.well-known/mcp/server-card.json | jq -e '.serverInfo.name or .name'
```

### 4.5 OpenAPI / API docs

- Stable ID: `ia.openapi`
- Stage: Act
- Strength: SHOULD
- AR practices: AR-ACT-02 (mapping: full)
- Evidence type: `measured_study`
- Fix: Publish an OpenAPI 3.x document at /openapi.json and link it.
- Fix workflow: [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md#ia.openapi)
- Evidence source: [agentready.org AR-ACT-02](https://www.agentready.org/#act)
- Applicability: detected_surface (api)
- Pass condition: OpenAPI 3.x document at a well-known location
- Expected result: exit code 0
- Rescan: `isagentready results {domain} --checkpoint ia.openapi`
- Details: https://isagentready.com/en/methodology/checkpoints/ia.openapi

Why: OpenAPI specifications let AI agents understand and call your API programmatically. AI coding assistants and agent frameworks use OpenAPI to generate correct API calls automatically.

References:

- [OpenAPI Specification](https://spec.openapis.org/oas/latest.html) (spec)
- [Swagger Editor](https://editor.swagger.io/) (guide)

Steps:

1. Generate an OpenAPI 3.1 document from the API code.

   ```json
   {
     "openapi": "3.1.0",
     "info": {"title": "Example API", "version": "1.0.0"},
     "paths": {"/api/search": {"get": {"operationId": "search", "summary": "Search items"}}}
   }
   ```
2. Serve it at /openapi.json or /.well-known/openapi with HTTP 200.
3. Link it from the API catalog and a service-desc Link header.

Verify:

```bash
curl -sf https://{domain}/openapi.json | jq -e '.openapi | startswith("3.")'
```

- Stage: Act
- Strength: SHOULD

<a id="ia.api-catalog"></a>

### 4.10 API Catalog (RFC 9727)

- Stable ID: `ia.api-catalog`
- Stage: Act
- Strength: SHOULD
- AR practices: AR-READ-06, AR-ACT-02 (mapping: full)
- Evidence type: `recommendation`
- Fix: Serve /.well-known/api-catalog as an application/linkset+json document.
- Fix workflow: [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md#ia.api-catalog)
- Evidence source: [agentready.org AR-READ-06](https://www.agentready.org/#read)
- Applicability: detected_surface (api)
- Expected result: exit code 0
- Rescan: `isagentready results {domain} --checkpoint ia.api-catalog`
- Details: https://isagentready.com/en/methodology/checkpoints/ia.api-catalog

Why: An API Catalog (RFC 9727 with an RFC 9264 linkset) gives agents one discovery endpoint for all APIs of the site. It links to OpenAPI documents, human docs and health endpoints.

References:

- [RFC 9727 API Catalog](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/rfc9727/) (spec)
- [RFC 9264 Linkset](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/rfc9264/) (spec)

Steps:

1. Create a linkset with one entry per API and service-desc, service-doc and status links.

   ```json
   {
     "linkset": [{
       "anchor": "https://example.com/api/v1",
       "service-desc": [{"href": "https://example.com/openapi.json", "type": "application/openapi+json"}],
       "service-doc": [{"href": "https://example.com/docs", "type": "text/html"}]
     }]
   }
   ```
2. Serve it at /.well-known/api-catalog with Content-Type application/linkset+json.

Verify:

```bash
curl -sf https://{domain}/.well-known/api-catalog | jq -e '.linkset | length > 0'
```

<a id="ia.agent-skills-index"></a>

### 4.11 Agent Skills index

- Stable ID: `ia.agent-skills-index`
- Stage: Act
- Strength: MAY
- AR practices: AR-ACT-06 (mapping: partial)
- Evidence type: `recommendation`
- Fix: Publish /.well-known/agent-skills/index.json with a digest for each skill.
- Fix workflow: [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md#ia.agent-skills-index)
- Evidence source: [agentready.org AR-ACT-06](https://www.agentready.org/#act)
- Applicability: detected_surface (api)
- Expected result: exit code 0
- Rescan: `isagentready results {domain} --checkpoint ia.agent-skills-index`
- Details: https://isagentready.com/en/methodology/checkpoints/ia.agent-skills-index

Why: An Agent Skills index lets a site publish a list of agent skills with SHA-256 digests of the SKILL.md content. Agents can then install and verify the skills.

References:

- [cloudflare/agent-skills-discovery-rfc](https://github.com/cloudflare/agent-skills-discovery-rfc) (guide)
- [agentskills.io](https://agentskills.io) (guide)

Steps:

1. Write a SKILL.md for each task that agents do on your site.
2. List the skills in the index with name, type, description, url and digest.

   ```json
   {
     "version": "0.2.0",
     "skills": [{
       "name": "search-products",
       "type": "skill-md",
       "description": "Search the product catalog",
       "url": "https://example.com/.well-known/agent-skills/search-products/SKILL.md",
       "digest": "sha256:<64 hex>"
     }]
   }
   ```

Verify:

```bash
curl -sf https://{domain}/.well-known/agent-skills/index.json | jq -e '.skills | length > 0'
```

<a id="ia.x402"></a>

### 4.12 x402 payments

- Stable ID: `ia.x402`
- Stage: Act
- Strength: MAY
- AR practices: AR-ACT-08 (mapping: partial)
- Evidence type: `recommendation`
- Fix: Return HTTP 402 with an x402 payment challenge on paid endpoints.
- Fix workflow: [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md#ia.x402)
- Evidence source: [agentready.org AR-ACT-08](https://www.agentready.org/#act)
- Applicability: detected_surface (commerce)
- Rescan: `isagentready results {domain} --checkpoint ia.x402`
- Details: https://isagentready.com/en/methodology/checkpoints/ia.x402

Why: The x402 protocol uses HTTP 402 Payment Required responses so agents can negotiate micropayments before consuming a paid API. A commerce site that supports x402 lets agents transact without manual checkout.

References:

- [x402 protocol](https://www.x402.org) (guide)

Steps:

1. Choose the paid endpoints and the price per call.
2. Return HTTP 402 with the x402 payment requirements when a request has no payment.

Verify:

No read-only shell check exists. Use the rescan command.

<a id="ia.mpp"></a>

### 4.13 MPP (x-payment-info)

- Stable ID: `ia.mpp`
- Stage: Act
- Strength: MAY
- AR practices: AR-ACT-08 (mapping: partial)
- Evidence type: `recommendation`
- Fix: Annotate paid OpenAPI operations with x-payment-info.
- Fix workflow: [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md#ia.mpp)
- Evidence source: [agentready.org AR-ACT-08](https://www.agentready.org/#act)
- Applicability: detected_surface (commerce)
- Expected result: exit code 0
- Rescan: `isagentready results {domain} --checkpoint ia.mpp`
- Details: https://isagentready.com/en/methodology/checkpoints/ia.mpp

Why: The Merchant Payments Protocol (MPP) extends OpenAPI with x-payment-info on individual operations so agents know which calls are paid and how to settle them.

References:

- [Merchant Payments Protocol](https://merchantpaymentsprotocol.org) (guide)

Steps:

1. Add an x-payment-info object to each paid operation in the OpenAPI document.

   ```json
   "x-payment-info": {"price": "0.01", "currency": "USD", "protocols": ["x402"]}
   ```

Verify:

```bash
curl -sf https://{domain}/openapi.json | jq -e '[.. | objects | has("x-payment-info")] | any'
```

<a id="ia.ap2"></a>

### 4.16 AP2

- Stable ID: `ia.ap2`
- Stage: Act
- Strength: MAY
- AR practices: AR-ACT-08 (mapping: partial)
- Evidence type: `recommendation`
- Fix: Add an AP2 entry to the extensions array of the A2A Agent Card.
- Fix workflow: [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md#ia.ap2)
- Evidence source: [agentready.org AR-ACT-08](https://www.agentready.org/#act)
- Applicability: detected_surface (commerce)
- Expected result: exit code 0
- Rescan: `isagentready results {domain} --checkpoint ia.ap2`
- Details: https://isagentready.com/en/methodology/checkpoints/ia.ap2

Why: Agent Payments Protocol (AP2) declares payment capability via the A2A Agent Card. The canonical encoding is an entry in the `extensions` array whose `uri` references AP2; agents inspect this array to know your service can transact.

References:

- [Google A2A Protocol](https://a2a-protocol.org/latest/specification/) (spec)
- [AP2 Agent Payments Protocol](https://github.com/google/A2A/blob/main/docs/payments.md) (guide)

Steps:

1. Add an extensions entry with a uri that points to the AP2 specification.

   ```json
   "extensions": [{"uri": "https://google.github.io/A2A/extensions/ap2", "required": false}]
   ```

Verify:

```bash
curl -sf https://{domain}/.well-known/agent-card.json | jq -e '[.extensions[]?.uri | test("ap2")] | any'
```

- Applicability: detected_surface (api, commerce)
- Expected result: exit code 0
- Rescan: `isagentready results {domain} --checkpoint ia.openapi-quality`
- Details: https://isagentready.com/en/methodology/checkpoints/ia.openapi-quality

Why: An OpenAPI document helps agents only when each operation is concrete. Agents need operationId, descriptions, typed parameters and response schemas to make a correct call.

References:

- [OpenAPI Specification](https://spec.openapis.org/oas/latest.html) (spec)

Steps:

1. Add a unique operationId and a description to each operation.
2. Add a schema with a type to each parameter and each response.

   ```json
   "parameters": [{"name": "q", "in": "query", "required": true, "schema": {"type": "string"}}]
   ```

Verify:

```bash
curl -sf https://{domain}/openapi.json | jq -e '[.paths[][] | objects | has("operationId")] | all'
```

<a id="ia.mcp-server-card"></a>

### 4.18 MCP server card quality

- Stable ID: `ia.mcp-server-card`
- Stage: Act
- Strength: MAY
- AR practices: AR-ACT-04 (mapping: full)
- Evidence type: `recommendation`
- Fix: Add serverInfo, a description, a transport, capabilities and auth to the server card.
- Fix workflow: [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md#ia.mcp-server-card)
- Evidence source: [agentready.org AR-ACT-04](https://www.agentready.org/#act)
- Applicability: detected_surface (api)
- Expected result: exit code 0
- Rescan: `isagentready results {domain} --checkpoint ia.mcp-server-card`
- Details: https://isagentready.com/en/methodology/checkpoints/ia.mcp-server-card

Why: An MCP server card should be actionable, not just discoverable. Agents need identity, transport, capabilities, and auth metadata before they can connect safely.

References:

- [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) (guide)
- [MCP specification](https://spec.modelcontextprotocol.io) (spec)
- [SEP-1649 server card](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/pull/2127) (guide)

Steps:

1. Complete the server card with all SEP-1649 fields.

   ```json
   {
     "serverInfo": {"name": "Example MCP", "version": "1.0.0"},
     "description": "Search and read product docs.",
     "transport": {"type": "streamable-http", "endpoint": "https://example.com/mcp"},
     "capabilities": {"tools": {}},
     "auth": {"type": "oauth2"}
   }
   ```

Verify:

```bash
curl -sf https://{domain}/.well-known/mcp/server-card.json | jq -e '.serverInfo and .transport and .capabilities'
```

<a id="ia.ai-catalog"></a>

### 4.21 AI Catalog

- Stable ID: `ia.ai-catalog`
- Stage: Find
- Strength: MAY
- AR practices: AR-FIND-04 (mapping: full)
- Evidence type: `recommendation`
- Fix: Publish /.well-known/ai-catalog.json and link it from the home page.
- Fix workflow: [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md#ia.ai-catalog)
- Evidence source: [agentready.org AR-FIND-04](https://www.agentready.org/#reachable)
- Applicability: always (website)
- Expected result: exit code 0
- Rescan: `isagentready results {domain} --checkpoint ia.ai-catalog`
- Details: https://isagentready.com/en/methodology/checkpoints/ia.ai-catalog

Why: An AI Catalog gives agents one machine-readable list of the AI resources of a site: MCP servers, APIs, skills and docs. Agents find it through links, so link it from the home page.

Steps:

1. Create /.well-known/ai-catalog.json with an entry for each MCP server, API, skill index and docs root.

   ```json
   {
     "name": "Example",
     "resources": [
       {"type": "mcp", "url": "https://example.com/mcp"},
       {"type": "openapi", "url": "https://example.com/openapi.json"}
     ]
   }
   ```
2. Serve the file as application/json with HTTP 200.
3. Link the catalog from the home page or from llms.txt.

Verify:

```bash
curl -sf https://{domain}/.well-known/ai-catalog.json | jq -e 'type == "object"'
```

<a id="ia.api-errors"></a>

### 4.22 API error responses

- Stable ID: `ia.api-errors`
- Stage: Act
- Strength: SHOULD
- AR practices: AR-ACT-02 (mapping: partial)
- Evidence type: `recommendation`
- Fix: Return RFC 9457 problem details as JSON for API errors.
- Fix workflow: [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md#ia.api-errors)
- Evidence source: [agentready.org AR-ACT-02](https://www.agentready.org/#act)
- Applicability: detected_surface (api)
- Expected result: exit code 0
- Rescan: `isagentready results {domain} --checkpoint ia.api-errors`
- Details: https://isagentready.com/en/methodology/checkpoints/ia.api-errors

Why: Agents call APIs programmatically and cannot recover from an HTML error page. A JSON problem-details body with a machine-readable code and a human-readable message lets them branch on failures instead of guessing.

References:

- [RFC 9457: Problem Details for HTTP APIs](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9457) (spec)

Steps:

1. Return application/problem+json for each 4xx and 5xx response of the API.

   ```json
   {"type": "https://example.com/problems/not-found", "title": "Not found", "status": 404, "detail": "No such resource"}
   ```

Verify:

```bash
curl -s https://{domain}/api/isagentready-missing-check | jq -e '.status or .error'
```

<a id="ia.api-rate-limits"></a>

### 4.23 API rate-limit headers

- Stable ID: `ia.api-rate-limits`
- Stage: Act
- Strength: MAY
- AR practices: AR-ACT-02 (mapping: partial)
- Evidence type: `recommendation`
- Fix: Send RateLimit and RateLimit-Policy headers on API responses.
- Fix workflow: [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md#ia.api-rate-limits)
- Evidence source: [agentready.org AR-ACT-02](https://www.agentready.org/#act)
- Applicability: detected_surface (api)
- Expected result: RateLimit or RateLimit-Policy headers
- Rescan: `isagentready results {domain} --checkpoint ia.api-rate-limits`
- Details: https://isagentready.com/en/methodology/checkpoints/ia.api-rate-limits

Why: Rate-limit headers let agents pace themselves before they hit a 429, and document the quota alongside the API instead of in prose only.

References:

- [Active Internet-Draft: RateLimit header fields for HTTP](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-ietf-httpapi-ratelimit-headers/) (spec)
- [RFC 9651: Structured Field Values for HTTP](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9651) (spec)
- [RFC 6585 section 4: 429 Too Many Requests](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6585#section-4) (spec)

Steps:

1. Add the IETF RateLimit and RateLimit-Policy headers to API responses.

   ```text
   RateLimit-Policy: "hourly";q=100;w=3600
   RateLimit: "hourly";r=42;t=1800
   ```
2. Add Retry-After to each 429 response.

Verify:

```bash
curl -sI https://{domain}/api/
```

<a id="ia.developer-docs-link"></a>

### 4.24 Developer docs discoverability

- Stable ID: `ia.developer-docs-link`
- Stage: Find
- Strength: MAY
- AR practices: AR-FIND-02, AR-READ-04 (mapping: partial)
- Evidence type: `measured_study`
- Fix: Link your developer documentation from the home page with a clear link text.
- Fix workflow: [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md#ia.developer-docs-link)
- Evidence source: [agentready.org AR-FIND-02](https://www.agentready.org/#reachable)
- Applicability: detected_surface (api, mcp)

- Rescan: `isagentready results {domain} --checkpoint ia.developer-docs-link`
- Details: https://isagentready.com/en/methodology/checkpoints/ia.developer-docs-link

Why: Agents and developers look for /docs, /developers or /api links on the home page to find how to integrate. An API that is only discoverable through well-known files is easy to miss.

References:

- [RFC 8288 service-doc link relation](https://www.iana.org/assignments/link-relations/link-relations.xhtml) (guide)

Steps:

1. Add a link to /docs or /developers in the main navigation or the footer.

   ```html
   <a href="/docs">Developer documentation</a>
   ```
2. Add a service-doc Link header that points to the same documentation.

   ```text
   Link: </docs>; rel="service-doc"
   ```

Verify:

```bash
curl -sI https://{domain}/docs
```

<a id="ia.mcp-apps"></a>

### 4.25 MCP Apps UI resources

- Stable ID: `ia.mcp-apps`
- Stage: Act
- Strength: MAY
- AR practices: AR-ACT-05 (mapping: full)
- Evidence type: `recommendation`
- Fix: Link each tool view to a ui:// resource and serve it with the MCP App media type.
- Fix workflow: [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md#ia.mcp-apps)
- Evidence source: [agentready.org AR-ACT-05](https://www.agentready.org/#act)
- Applicability: detected_surface (mcp)
- Pass condition: A tool with _meta.ui.resourceUri or a ui:// resource that reads as text/html;profile=mcp-app. The scanner sends one read-only JSON-RPC resources/read POST inside the verified 4.20 session. This is the only POST of the coverage checks.
- Rescan: `isagentready results {domain} --checkpoint ia.mcp-apps`
- Details: https://isagentready.com/en/methodology/checkpoints/ia.mcp-apps

Why: MCP Apps let an agent host show an interactive view of a tool result. The host can render the view only when the server links a ui:// resource and serves it as text/html;profile=mcp-app.

References:

- [MCP Apps extension (SEP-1865)](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps) (spec)
- [agentready.org AR-ACT-05](https://www.agentready.org/#act) (guide)

Steps:

1. Add _meta.ui.resourceUri with a ui:// URI to each tool that has a view.

   ```json
   {"name": "show_chart", "_meta": {"ui": {"resourceUri": "ui://charts/view"}}}
   ```
2. Answer resources/read for that URI with mimeType text/html;profile=mcp-app and the HTML in text.

Verify:

No read-only shell check exists. Use the rescan command.

### 4.26 NLWeb ask endpoint

- Stable ID: `ia.nlweb-ask`
- Stage: Act
- Strength: MAY
- AR practices: AR-ACT-09 (mapping: full)
- Evidence type: `recommendation`
- Fix: Serve NLWeb at /ask with schema.org results.
- Fix workflow: [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md#ia.nlweb-ask)
- Evidence source: [agentready.org AR-ACT-09](https://www.agentready.org/#act)
- Applicability: always (website)
- Pass condition: GET /ask?query=... returns JSON with a results array of schema.org objects
- Expected result: exit code 0
- Rescan: `isagentready results {domain} --checkpoint ia.nlweb-ask`
- Details: https://isagentready.com/en/methodology/checkpoints/ia.nlweb-ask

Why: NLWeb lets an agent ask a site a question and get schema.org results back. A working /ask endpoint gives agents a direct answer path instead of a crawl. The check is informational and gives no points.

References:

- [NLWeb](https://github.com/nlweb-ai/NLWeb) (spec)
- [agentready.org AR-ACT-09](https://www.agentready.org/#act) (guide)

<a id="ia.agent-checkout"></a>

### 4.27 Agent checkout

- Stable ID: `ia.agent-checkout`
- Stage: Act
- Strength: MAY
- AR practices: AR-ACT-08 (mapping: full)
- Evidence type: `measured_study`
- Fix: Give agents a payment path at checkout.
- Fix workflow: [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md#ia.agent-checkout)
- Evidence source: [agentready.org AR-ACT-08](https://www.agentready.org/#act)
- Applicability: detected_surface (commerce)
- Pass condition: A Stripe Link or Shared Payment Token marker at checkout, or checkout_sessions in /.well-known/acp.json
- Expected result: exit code 0
- Rescan: `isagentready results {domain} --checkpoint ia.agent-checkout`
- Details: https://isagentready.com/en/methodology/checkpoints/ia.agent-checkout

Why: Agents finish a purchase only when the checkout accepts an agent payment path. In the agentready.org study, agents completed Link checkouts correctly in most cases. The check looks for Stripe Link, Shared Payment Tokens or an ACP checkout_sessions endpoint, and never sends a POST.

References:

- [agentready.org AR-ACT-08](https://www.agentready.org/#act) (study)
- [Agentic Commerce Protocol](https://www.agenticcommerce.dev) (spec)
- [Stripe agentic commerce](https://docs.stripe.com/agentic-commerce) (guide)

Steps:

1. Accept Stripe Link or Shared Payment Tokens on the checkout page.
2. Declare the checkout_sessions endpoint in /.well-known/acp.json.

   ```json
   {"flows": ["checkout"], "capabilities": {"checkout": {"endpoint": "https://example.com/acp/checkout_sessions"}}}
   ```

Verify:

```bash
curl -s https://{domain}/.well-known/acp.json | grep -q checkout_sessions
```

### 4.28 SDKs and CLI

- Stable ID: `ia.sdk-cli`

- AR practices: AR-ACT-06 (mapping: full)

- Details: https://isagentready.com/en/methodology/checkpoints/ia.sdk-cli

Why: An official SDK or CLI gives agents tested calls, auth handling and clear errors. Agents that find one in the docs or in llms.txt finish tasks with fewer failed requests.

References:

- [agentready.org AR-ACT-06](https://www.agentready.org/#act) (guide)

Steps:

   ```

Verify:

```

<a id="ia.docs-answer"></a>

### 4.30 Docs pages that answer

- Stable ID: `ia.docs-answer`
- Stage: Read
- Strength: SHOULD
- AR practices: AR-READ-04, AR-FIND-02, AR-READ-05 (mapping: full)
- Evidence type: `measured_study`
- Fix: Render docs pages on the server with headings and language-tagged code.
- Fix workflow: [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md#ia.docs-answer)
- Evidence source: [agentready.org AR-READ-04](https://www.agentready.org/#read)
- Applicability: detected_surface (api, mcp)
- Pass condition: Docs pages with HTTP 200, server-rendered text, a heading structure and language-tagged code blocks
- Expected result: a count above 0
- Rescan: `isagentready results {domain} --checkpoint ia.docs-answer`
- Details: https://isagentready.com/en/methodology/checkpoints/ia.docs-answer

Why: Agents read docs pages as raw HTML and reuse code from them. In the agentready.org study, agents reached docs pages in most runs. A page that needs JavaScript, has no headings or shows untagged code gives the agent no usable answer.

References:

- [agentready.org AR-READ-04](https://www.agentready.org/#read) (study)
- [agentready.org AR-READ-05](https://www.agentready.org/#read) (study)

Steps:

1. Render the docs text in the server HTML, with at least a few paragraphs per page.
2. Give each page an h1 and h2 or h3 headings.
3. Tag each code block with its language.

   ```html
   <pre><code class="language-bash">curl https://api.example.com/v1/items</code></pre>
   ```

Verify:

```bash
curl -sL https://{domain}/docs | grep -c 'class="language-'
```
